learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the incredible backstage journey of how a written story transforms into a spectacular live stage performance using blocking, props, and rehearsals!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Blocking is the stage choreography of a play. It decides where actors stand, when they walk, and how they interact so the audience can clearly see and understand the action.
Props are the objects actors hold, like a mysterious letter, a walking stick, or a glowing sword. These objects make the imaginary world feel totally real and help actors tell the story.
A brilliant play is built during rehearsals. This is where actors memorize lines, try out different expressions, make funny mistakes, and learn to work together as a powerful team.

fun_activity.title: 🌂 The Magic Prop Box
fun_activity.instructions: Find three random objects in your room like a ruler, a hat, and a mug. Invent a mini-scene where these everyday items are actually magical artifacts used by a secret spy!

quick_recap: ⭐ Blocking tells actors exactly where to move on stage so the performance looks organized and beautiful.
⭐ Props are physical items that help bring the story to life and make the actor's actions more believable.
⭐ Rehearsals are the safe space where actors practice, fail, try again, and finally perfect their stage magic.
